artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary $\partial\Omega = \overline{\Gamma_D} \cup \overline{\Gamma_T}$, where $\Gamma_D$ and $\Gamma_T$ are disjoint relatively open subsets on which displacement and traction boundary conditions are imposed, respectively, and whose closures meet along a (nonempty) interface $\overline{\Gamma_D}\cap\overline{\Gamma_T}$. Consider a hyperelastic body occupying $\Omega$ in its reference configuration with a frame-indifferent, polyconvex (or otherwise physically reasonable) stored-energy function $W:\Omega\times M^{3\times 3}_+\to\mathbb{R}$, and the associated equilibrium equations 
$$\operatorname{Div}\,DW(x,\nabla u(x)) + \lambda\, b(x,u,\lambda) = 0 \quad\text{in }\Omega,$$
$$u = u_0(\lambda) \text{ on }\Gamma_D, \qquad DW(x,\nabla u)\nu = t(\lambda) \text{ on }\Gamma_T,$$
depending on a real (loading) parameter $\lambda$.

Develop local and global bifurcation theories for this mixed displacement-traction problem that:
(a) provide rigorous criteria, in terms of the linearization at a trivial branch $u=u(\lambda)$, for the existence of local bifurcating branches of equilibria;
(b) yield global continuation results (in the style of Rabinowitz) for connected components of nontrivial solutions, valid despite the loss of regularity at the interface $\overline{\Gamma_D}\cap\overline{\Gamma_T}$;
(c) apply in particular to three-dimensional buckling problems (e.g., buckling of a clamped/loaded elastic block or column) where mixed boundary conditions of this type are unavoidable.

Specifically, identify functional-analytic settings and hypotheses on $W$, $\Omega$, $\Gamma_D$, $\Gamma_T$, and the loadings under which standard tools (Fredholm theory, transversality, degree theory) can be made to work, or otherwise devise an alternative approach that circumvents the regularity loss at the boundary interface.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find a published resolution of this problem. Local and global bifurcation theory for three-dimensional nonlinear elastostatics with mixed displacement–traction boundary conditions and meeting boundary portions is widely regarded as still open, owing to the loss of elliptic regularity at the interface; partial results exist for pure displacement or pure traction problems and for smooth boundaries, but not for the general mixed case.
